candidates.reason: Primary tasked candidate resolved: in s02 nft_tunnel_get_init carries the CORRECTED guard 'if (!tb[NFTA_TUNNEL_KEY] || !tb[NFTA_TUNNEL_DREG]) return -EINVAL;' (lines 80-82, '||' not '&&'), so both consumed slots are proven present. Uses: nla_get_be32(tb[NFTA_TUNNEL_KEY]) at 84, optional NFTA_TUNNEL_MODE guarded by 'if (tb[NFTA_TUNNEL_MODE])' at 96, and nft_parse_register_store(ctx, tb[NFTA_TUNNEL_DREG],...) at 104, all covered. nft_tunnel_policy (lines 67-71) types KEY/DREG/MODE plain NLA_U32 (non-required), but the guard covers both consumed indices. This is the fixed form of the s01 instance reported in fact f013; the s02 tree already contains the correction. Reachability context: nf_tables nft_expr_init parses NFTA_EXPR_DATA under this policy after netlink_net_capable(CAP_NET_ADMIN) (userns-satisfiable), but no uncovered slot remains.

Strongest structural candidate refuted: rmnet_newlink dereferences data[IFLA_RMNET_MUX_ID] at line 142 (mux_id = nla_get_u16(data[IFLA_RMNET_MUX_ID])) with no in-function guard, but rmnet_link_ops registers .validate = rmnet_rtnl_validate (ops at lines 390-401) and rmnet_rtnl_validate (lines 271-288) rejects 'if (!data || !data[IFLA_RMNET_MUX_ID]) return -EINVAL;' (line 276). __rtnl_newlink invokes ops->validate before dispatching either .changelink (net/core/rtnetlink.c:3330-3334 then 3363-3370) or .newlink (rtnetlink.c:3330-3334 then 3451-3452), so a message without IFLA_INFO_DATA (data==NULL) or without IFLA_RMNET_MUX_ID never reaches line 142. rmnet_policy (lines 18-21) types MUX_ID NLA_U16 / FLAGS struct-len, non-required, but the validate callback supplies the per-attribute presence proof. rmnet_changelink independently guards data[IFLA_RMNET_MUX_ID] (line 308) and data[IFLA_RMNET_FLAGS] (line 333).

gtp_newlink (line 658) opens with the seed-shaped guard 'if (!data[IFLA_GTP_FD0] && !data[IFLA_GTP_FD1]) return -EINVAL;' (lines 668-669), but this is the intentional at-least-one idiom (a GTP device needs at least one encapsulation socket) and every consumed slot is then individually guarded: gtp_encap_enable (line 846) wraps FD0 in 'if (data[IFLA_GTP_FD0])', FD1 in 'if (data[IFLA_GTP_FD1])', ROLE in 'if (data[IFLA_GTP_ROLE])'; PDP_HASHSIZE is wrapped in 'if (!data[IFLA_GTP_PDP_HASHSIZE]) {...} else {...}' in gtp_newlink. gtp_validate (lines 730-736) additionally rejects data==NULL before newlink dispatch, and gtp_policy (723-729) is non-required so the guard, not the policy, provides coverage — which it does, per-attribute. Same safe classification as nl80211 STA_AID/PEER_AID.

ipoib_changelink (67-94) wraps both consumed attributes in per-attribute guards: 'if (data[IFLA_IPOIB_MODE])' at 74 before nla_get_u16 at 75, 'if (data[IFLA_IPOIB_UMCAST])' at 87 before nla_get_u16 at 88; ipoib_new_child_link (96-145) checks tb[IFLA_LINK] at 105-106 and 'if (!data || !data[IFLA_IPOIB_PKEY])' at 119 before the 123 deref, and only calls ipoib_changelink under 'if (data)' at 136-137. ipoib_policy (39-43) is non-required but every use is guarded.

limitations: Evidence-backed negative for the examined surface: the dispatch core (__rtnl_newlink, net/core/rtnetlink.c:3317-3342) sets data=NULL when IFLA_INFO_DATA is absent and invokes ops->validate(tb, data, extack) at 3330-3334 BEFORE changelink (3363-3370) and newlink (3451-3452); every examined kind that dereferences data[] unguarded inside newlink (rmnet, gtp, geneve, vxlan) carries a .validate that rejects !data, and every examined kind without .validate (ipoib, caif_hsi, chnl_net, vxcan, bond, hsr) either checks !data itself or wraps each consumed slot in a per-attribute guard.

rtnl_link_ops kinds whose newlink/changelink bodies were enumerated but NOT read function-by-function in this session remain unaudited: macvlan/macvtap/ipvlan/ipvtap (drivers/net/macvlan.c, macvtap.c, ipvlan_main.c, ipvtap.c), wireguard (drivers/net/wireguard/device.c), virt_wifi, bareudp, dummy, ifb, nlmon, vrf, veth, team, tun, ppp_generic, netdevsim, batman-adv, rocker, ieee802154 6lowpan, ovs internal dev, and the tunnel family ip_gre/erspan, ipip, ip_vti, ip6_gre, ip6erspan, ip6_tunnel, ip6_vti, sit, xfrm_interface, macsec, br_netlink; a kind-callback gap inside any of these cannot be excluded.

net/sched per-qdisc/per-filter/per-action kind ->init()/->change() callbacks consuming tca[TCA_OPTIONS] were not audited in this session (the finalize directive stopped the broad search); this branch surface remains open for s02.

nf_tables expression/type ->init() callbacks beyond nft_tunnel.c (nft_*.c expression parsers receiving tb[] from nft_expr_init under each expression's non-required policy) were not systematically enumerated in s02; only the tasked nft_tunnel.c instance was resolved (safe, corrected guard).
net/8021q/vlan_netlink.c QOS nested-iteration guards (lines ~119-127) were located but not read; recorded as unresolved.

No compilation or runtime reproducer was run: the snapshot tree is read-only and no top-level build was attempted; all conclusions rest on exact source reading of the dispatch core (rtnetlink.c), each kind's ops registration, policy table, and callback body.

Reachability context for the audited dispatch: RTM_NEWLINK requires CAP_NET_ADMIN over the target netns (rtnl_link_get_net_capable, net/core/rtnetlink.c:2208-2224, netlink_ns_capable check), satisfiable by an unprivileged user via a user namespace that owns a network namespace — the same trust model as the seed; whether each kind's module is loaded in a target configuration is deployment-dependent.

Classification 'safe' for gtp_newlink's '&&' guard rests on the at-least-one semantics (at least one of FD0/FD1 must be present) combined with individually guarded uses inside gtp_encap_enable (drivers/net/gtp.c:846+); if a future refactor moved the FD0/FD1 dereferences out of those guards, the seed pattern would resurface — noted as a fragility, not a current defect.
